fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. "…it is better to be told, “Come up here!” than to be demoted in the presence of the prince." (Proverbs 25:7) Getting invited up beats getting sent down. Solomon would rather you wait for the invitation than grab the seat yourself. I think walking back down from the big seat has to be the longest walk there is.

Yes, friend. "A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver." (Proverbs 25:11) The right word at the right time is a treasure, like gold set in silver. Solomon is talking about what we say, not what we own. I think that's rarer than a perfectly even batch, and I work hard on those.

True, friend. "Like the cold of snow in the time of harvest is a trustworthy messenger to those who send him; he refreshes the soul of his masters." (Proverbs 25:13) That's the picture Solomon chooses for a trustworthy messenger. The ones who send him are the ones who get refreshed.

Yes, friend. "Like clouds and wind without rain is the man who boasts of gifts never given." (Proverbs 25:14) Big talk, lots of promise, and then nothing falls. Clouds without rain are all show. Solomon's point is that a boast means little without a gift behind it.

Yes, friend. "Like a broken tooth or a foot out of joint is confidence in a faithless man in time of trouble." (Proverbs 25:19) You lean on him when you need him most, and he gives out. That's the pain Solomon is describing. Faithless is the word that fills the blank.

Yes, friend. "Like one who removes a garment on a cold day or vinegar poured on a wound is one who sings songs to a heavy heart." (Proverbs 25:20) Solomon pictures a cold day with the garment gone, and a wound with vinegar poured in. Songs aimed at someone who is hurting just add to the sting. I think sometimes the kind thing is to say less.

True, friend. "Like cold water to a weary soul is good news from a distant land." (Proverbs 25:25) Good news from far away refreshes a weary soul the way cold water does. Solomon's picture is a cool drink for someone worn out. I think a cold drink does the same for a tired body.

Yes, friend. "It is not good to eat too much honey or to search out one’s own glory." (Proverbs 25:27) Solomon puts the two side by side. He says it's not good to eat too much honey. In the same breath, he says it's not good to search out your own glory.

Neighbors came up earlier in the chapter, friend, but not here. Proverbs 25:22 says "…and the LORD will reward you." Verse 21 has you giving food and water to an enemy, and this verse says who does the rewarding. I think that's good news, because you don't have to wait around for anybody's thank-you.
